A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an unsupervised learning approach to learn goal spaces from passive observations of world changes.
we show that the goal space can be learned by a robot in a developmental way, and that it is sufficient to achieve the same level of skill acquisition as if the goal space had been engineered.
we propose a new way to learn a goal representation for goal exploration algorithms, which is a key component of intrinsically motivated goal-directed learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible for a robot to autonomously learn a goal space that allows it to discover a repertoire of skills that it could use for future goal-directed behaviors.
the use of deep representation learning algorithms for the purpose of goal exploration in intrinsically motivated agents is a promising direction for the field.
it is feasible to learn goal spaces that are adequate for goal exploration in high-dimensional environments, and that this can lead to better performance than hand-engineering goal representations.
